#  🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing 
 Yiwen Song 1 , Yale Song 1 , Tomas Pfister 1 , and Jinsung Yoon 1  
  1 Google Cloud AI Research 
PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams.
Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
## Key Features
- **Multi-Agent Pipeline**: Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation.
- **Comprehensive Literature Synthesis**: Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript.
- **Visuals Generation**: Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams.
- **LaTeX Automation**: Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates.
## Installation
1.  **Environment Setup**: The project relies on a Conda environment named `paper_orchestra`. You can set up a similar environment with Python 3.11 and install the required dependencies.

    conda create -n paper

# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序
   English  ·  简体中文 (Chinese)  ·  繁體中文 (Traditional Chinese)  ·  日本語 (Japanese) 
**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History**
[**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en)
*The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*
---
## Why It's Fun to Explore
Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry:
- *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"*
- *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"*
- *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?
itens.desc_pt: Mapa interativo com mais de dois mil anos de história da China, ano a ano.

# Superpowers
Superpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.

## How it works
It starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. 
Once it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest.

Svelte is a new way to build web applications. It's a compiler that takes your declarative components and converts them into efficient JavaScript that surgically updates the DOM.
Learn more at the [Svelte website](https://svelte.dev), or stop by the [Discord chatroom](https://svelte.dev/chat).

Svelte is an MIT-licensed open source project with its ongoing development made possible entirely by fantastic volunteers. If you'd like to support their efforts, please consider:

Funds donated via Open Collective will be used for compensating expenses related to Svelte's development such as hosting costs. If sufficient donations are received, funds may also be used to support Svelte's development more directly.
